entries.speaker: narrator
lines: One throne of death stands empty. Strange — the instant its lord fell, I felt you grow heavier in my boat. More real. More HERE.

A hundred generations I have poled this ferry across the Styx, taking my coin from beneath each dead tongue. Yours carried no coin, and no name in my ledger — and the lords of the dead were set to GUARD something. I had forgotten that.
Forgotten it, as though the dark itself wished me to forget.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Two lords cast down, and with each, a memory rises in you — a face, a shore, a name half-spoken. You were mortal once; that much is plain.
The islanders call it rwa bhineda — the seen and the unseen held in balance, so that neither may win. These six realms are that veil, drawn in six colours over a single wound.
You are pulling the veil back, wanderer. I am no longer certain you should.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: I remember you now. You died — and you RAN. From the scales of Anubis, from the feather of Ma'at, from every judgment laid before you.
So no afterlife could keep you whole; each one tore away a shard of your soul as you fled. Three shards reclaimed now. Three remain.
But understand what the lords truly are. Not kings of the dead. Wardens. Jailers. And the cell they keep has begun, very slowly, to stir.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Four shards. You stand almost whole — and almost whole, you feel it too, do you not? That slow tide far below. That breathing beneath the floor of every underworld.
The lords dreaded the weighing of YOUR heart because your heart is the crack — the first soul that ever refused to lie still in the earth. The flaw the sleeper dreams through.
Two deaths remain. After them, there is nowhere left to look but down.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: One shard remains, held by the last warden of the dead. Take it, and you will be whole — name, deeds, weight, and all.

And whole, you will understand why six pantheons chained their own gods to thrones they despised. Hel's grey gate, Mictlan's ninefold pit, sunken R'lyeh — one grave, seen through different eyes, and each god a nail in its lid.
There is no more running, wanderer. Only the road — and the thing at the bottom of it, listening now for your footsteps.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: It is done. Six wardens of death lie behind you. Six locks, broken by your hand. You are whole at last — you remember your name, and the weight of it.
I told you the light above was freedom. I lied — as the dark has made me lie since the beginning. That light was never a door OUT.
It is the lid of a tomb, lifting. And below — far beneath all six underworlds — something that has dreamed since before the first death opens one vast and patient eye.
The gods who judged you now hide their faces. They built the whole machinery of death to hold this grave shut, and you took it apart trial by trial, believing you were saving only yourself.
To break the cycle was to break the seal. A seventh door stands open now — R'lyeh, the wound beneath the wounds. It was never meant to be found. Go down, wanderer. Finish what your refusal began.
